title: TokMem: Tokenized Procedural Memory for Large Language Models
one_liner: TokMem stores reusable procedures in compact learned memory slots so a language model can invoke them without rereading a long prompt at every step.
lead: Large language models often rely on long prompts to describe a task, a workflow, or a tool-usage procedure. That is wasteful because the model must reread the same instructions again and again as generation continues. This paper proposes TokMem, a procedural memory system that stores reusable procedures as compact learned memory slots. The base model stays frozen, new procedures can be added later, and the memory slot both points to the right procedure and steers generation toward using it.

problem.h2: Prompting repeats the same instructions over and over
paras: A language model can follow a procedure such as 'call this tool, parse the result, then answer in this format' if that procedure is written into the prompt. The problem is that the procedure must sit in the context window while the model works through the task.

That repeated context is expensive and hard to scale. As more tasks and procedures accumulate, prompts become longer, slower, and harder to reuse. Standard fine-tuning has a different problem: it changes the model weights directly, which makes incremental updates harder and risks interfering with older capabilities.

callout.html: Reusable procedures live either in long prompts or in model weights. The paper wants a middle layer that is compact, modular, and addable over time.

hidden.h2: The hidden quantity: procedure reuse density
hidden.name: how much reusable instruction can be packed into a compact memory slot
paras: The important hidden quantity is procedure reuse density: how much task guidance can be stored in a small learned slot instead of a long prompt. If this density is high, the slot carries enough information to trigger a useful workflow even though it is tiny compared with the original prompt.

The paper estimates this quantity indirectly by measuring task success under fixed-size memory slots. If a short slot consistently replaces a much longer prompt while keeping or improving performance, then the slot is storing reusable procedural guidance rather than acting as a weak hint.

heat.caption: Darker cells indicate memory slots that carry enough procedural guidance to replace much longer prompt instructions.

reads.html: This asks how much reusable know-how a compact memory slot can carry.
The paper studies whether a compact learned procedure representation can support atomic and compositional recall with constant context overhead.

mechanism.h2: Why compact procedural memory can beat repeated prompting
paras: A long prompt works because it repeatedly reminds the model of what procedure to follow. But that repetition burns context and compute at every generation step. TokMem moves the reusable part into a compact learned slot, so the procedure is injected once in a form the model can directly use.

The backbone model remains frozen, which matters for continual updates. New procedures can be added by training new slots instead of editing the entire model. That avoids interference with older procedures because the base model weights stay fixed while the new procedural control lives in its own small memory object.

The slot plays two roles at once. It identifies the relevant procedure and also pushes generation toward following that procedure. This dual role is why the method can outperform retrieval-augmented prompting on procedural tasks, because the model does not just read retrieved text; it receives a learned control signal tailored to execution.

math.words: Pick the procedure slot whose learned score is largest for the current task, then use that slot to steer generation.
symbols: the current task description or state
how well slot s matches the procedure needed for the task

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose the model has three procedure slots: tool use, factual recall, and multi-step function calling.
For a new task, the matching scores are 0.20, 0.15, and 0.77.
The system picks the multi-step function-calling slot because 0.77 is the largest score.
That slot is inserted once and guides the model through the needed procedure.
The long instruction prompt is no longer needed at every step because the compact slot carries the reusable control.

math.note: The exact internal representation can be more detailed, but the conceptual rule is simple: select the procedure slot that best matches the current task.

charts.title: Prompting or retrieval baseline
charts.note: Repeated prompt text keeps overhead high and does not provide a dedicated procedural control signal.

charts.title: TokMem
charts.note: Compact slots improve procedural reuse because the learned memory carries workflow guidance without a long repeated prompt.

items.html: If the system picks the wrong procedure slot, the model may confidently follow an irrelevant workflow because the control signal points in the wrong direction.
If a slot is too compact for the workflow it is meant to store, it may carry only partial guidance, so task quality can drop.

The method helps most when the task matches a recurring workflow because the stored slot already contains the needed procedural guidance. A truly new procedure still needs either a new slot or ordinary prompting.
With good slot selection and enough capacity per slot, TokMem improves reuse because it stores recurring procedures in a modular layer that can be added without rewriting the base model.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Take a frozen language model and define several recurring workflows, such as direct factual lookup, multi-step tool use, and short function-call chains. Train compact procedure slots for each workflow. Compare three setups on held-out tasks: long prompting, retrieval-style inserted instructions, and TokMem slots.
demo.closing: The demo should show that compact procedural memory improves reuse because the model can invoke a stored workflow without rereading a long instruction block at every generation step.
